_comment: Shared DSQL write contract: the canonical target encoding for each boundary MySQL type, loaded by BOTH the Python bulk-loader parity test (tests/test_dsql_write_contract.py) and the Java sink parity test (DebeziumTypeConverterTest). One artifact governs both write paths so the same source row lands identically whether migrated by Full Load (Python) or CDC (Java). Mirror of converter.DSQL_WRITE_CONTRACT_CASES. Do not edit one language's copy in isolation -- this file is copied to connectors/dsql-sink/src/test/resources/ by the Java build/test setup.

cases.name: datetime
cases.note: Long millis-since-epoch -> java.time.LocalDateTime (the UTC wall clock), bound as timestamp. Python bulk loader writes the naive datetime(2024-01-01 00:00:00).

cases.name: datetime6
cases.note: Long micros-since-epoch -> java.time.LocalDateTime (the UTC wall clock), microseconds preserved. This is the H5 bug: setObject(Long) to a TIMESTAMP column was rejected with SQLSTATE 42804.

cases.name: timestamp_tz
cases.note: ISO-8601 string -> java.time.OffsetDateTime at UTC, bound as timestamptz.

cases.name: datetime_year_0001
cases.note: .NET DateTime.MinValue / Go zero time. Arrives as the year 1 only with Debezium enable.time.adjuster=false (set on the cdc-stack MySQL source; the default reads a year 0-99 as 2000-2069 / 1970-1999). Bound as a java.sql.Timestamp it was rendered by pgjdbc in the Julian calendar before 1582-10-15 and sent as 0001-01-03.

cases.name: datetime6_year_1000
cases.note: MySQL's documented DATETIME minimum, a common 'no date' value. Bound as a java.sql.Timestamp it was sent as 0999-12-27; on a key the upsert inserted a second row and the delete matched nothing.

cases.name: datetime6_1582_10_04
cases.note: The last day before the Gregorian reform. Bound as a java.sql.Timestamp it was sent as 1582-09-24; from 1582-10-15 on it was always exact.

cases.name: date_1582_10_05
cases.note: Epoch day -> java.time.LocalDate, bound as date in the proleptic calendar. 1582-10-05 .. 1582-10-14 are the ten days the Gregorian reform skipped: bound as a java.sql.Date, which pgjdbc renders through a GregorianCalendar, each was sent ten days later (this one as 1582-10-15); on a key the upsert inserted a second row and the delete matched nothing.

cases.name: date_1582_10_10
cases.note: A skipped day; as a java.sql.Date it was sent as 1582-10-20.

cases.name: date_1582_10_14
cases.note: The last skipped day; as a java.sql.Date it was sent as 1582-10-24. Before 1582-10-05 and from 1582-10-15 on, the java.sql.Date was exact.

cases.name: date_year_0001
cases.note: .NET DateTime.MinValue / Go zero time as a DATE. Arrives as the year 1 only with Debezium enable.time.adjuster=false (set on the cdc-stack MySQL source).

cases.name: date_year_1000
cases.note: MySQL's documented DATE minimum, a common 'no date' value.

cases.name: bigint_unsigned
cases.note: 2^64-1; requires bigint.unsigned.handling.mode=precise so Debezium sends a BigDecimal, not an overflowing Long. Binds to numeric(20,0).

cases.name: decimal
cases.note: Debezium precise mode sends BigDecimal; binds to numeric. No conversion needed at the sink (passes through).

cases.name: tinyint_one
cases.note: MySQL boolean convention; 1 -> True, 0 -> False. Python: bool(int(v)).

cases.name: blob
cases.note: byte[] passes through; setObject(byte[]) -> bytea. Python: bytes(v).

cases.name: json
cases.note: JSON text must be wrapped in a PGobject(type=json) so the JDBC driver targets the json column, not text. Python passes the string through (psycopg handles json).

cases.name: enum
cases.note: ENUM -> text; both paths keep the string.
